title: Five Sixes in an Over: Marcus Stoinis Rips Washington Freedom Apart as Seattle Orcas Cruise to an 88-Run MLC Victory
excerpt: Shimron Hetmyer's nine-six blitz and Jasdeep Singh's five-wicket masterclass power the biggest win of MLC 2026 at the Oakland Coliseum
body:
Some overs are routine. Some are memorable. And then there are overs that make everyone in the ground — and everyone watching at home — stand up and stare.

Marcus Stoinis delivered that kind of over on Friday at the Oakland Coliseum. The Seattle Orcas captain smashed five sixes off Ian Holland in a single, devastating 17th over that yielded 30 runs, turned a strong total into an imposing one, and left Washington Freedom captain Steve Smith visibly stunned in the field.

It was the centrepiece of MLC 2026's most lopsided result so far — an 88-run annihilation that underscored just how dangerous this Seattle side can be when their big names fire together.

## Hetmyer sets the table, Stoinis flips it

Stoinis's explosion did not come from nowhere. The platform was built by Shimron Hetmyer, who played one of the innings of the tournament — an unbeaten 79 off just 33 balls, laced with nine sixes and two fours. The Guyanese left-hander arrived with Seattle needing acceleration and responded with clean, brutal hitting that Washington's bowlers simply had no answer for.

Tim Seifert gave the innings a solid foundation at the top with a brisk 37 off 20 balls. But it was Hetmyer and Stoinis who transformed a competitive score into an unreachable one: 227 for 6 in 20 overs.



> **"The platform was built by Shimron Hetmyer, who played one of the innings of the tournament — an unbeaten 79 off just 33 balls, laced with nine sixes and two fours."**


Stoinis himself finished with 42 off 16 balls and six sixes in total — five of them coming in that extraordinary Holland over. The Australian all-rounder had been scratchy early, scoring just four from his first six deliveries, before flicking a switch that turned the contest on its head. Holland, who had conceded only 19 from his first three overs, ended with figures of 3 for 49 — his economy wrecked in the space of six balls.

## Jasdeep Singh makes it a rout


![Ian Holland — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ab/2_12_Ian_Holland.jpg)


If the batting set up the win, the bowling sealed it beyond any doubt. Jasdeep Singh, the Indian-origin fast bowler, tore through Washington's top order with a spell that reduced the Freedom to 50 for 7. Glenn Maxwell and Steve Smith — Washington's two most dangerous batters — both fell cheaply as Singh found pace, bounce, and movement from the Oakland surface.

His final figures of 5 for 24 were the best of MLC 2026 so far, and they effectively ended the contest before it had properly begun. Amila Aponso's rapid 31 off 13 balls offered a brief, violent counterattack, but it was too little and far too late. Cameron Gannon mopped up the tail with 2 for 16, and Washington were bowled out for 139 in just 16.2 overs — 88 runs short of the target.

## What this means for the table

The win lifts Seattle to joint-top of the MLC 2026 standings alongside Texas Super Kings, both on four points from four matches. Washington Freedom, who had shown flashes of competitiveness earlier in the tournament with Rachin Ravindra and Maxwell in their ranks, slip to the bottom half with just two points from three games.

For Seattle, the timing could not be better. MLC's Oakland Coliseum weekend continues with further matches on Saturday and Sunday, and a squad firing on all cylinders — Hetmyer with the bat, Singh with the ball, and Stoinis capable of changing a match in a single over — is a formidable prospect for every other team in the competition.

## Cricket at the Coliseum — and what it means for the diaspora

The Oakland Coliseum, once home to the A's and the Raiders, hosting professional cricket is still a surreal sight for many longtime Bay Area residents. But for the region's substantial South Asian community, it represents a statement of arrival. MLC's third season has brought bigger venues, deeper squads, and steadily improving production — and the presence of Indian-heritage players like Jasdeep Singh, Harmeet Singh, Sujit Nayak, and several others across the league's rosters gives NRI fans in the Bay Area and beyond a direct connection to the action.

Friday's match was the kind of spectacle that draws converts. Five sixes in an over. A five-wicket haul. An 88-run margin. If American cricket needed a highlight reel, Marcus Stoinis and Jasdeep Singh handed it one — right in the heart of Silicon Valley's backyard.

**Brief scores:** Seattle Orcas 227/6 in 20 overs (Shimron Hetmyer 79* off 33b, Marcus Stoinis 42 off 16b, Tim Seifert 37 off 20b; Marco Jansen 3/49) beat Washington Freedom 139 all out in 16.2 overs (Amila Aponso 31 off 13b, Ian Holland 26; Jasdeep Singh 5/24, Cameron Gannon 2/16) by 88 runs.
